statement: The labelled cyclic 3-root system has exactly 6 distinct complex solutions, all of multiplicity one.

answer.multiplicity: Every solution has intersection multiplicity one.

source.location: Introduction, printed p.2: table of γ(n) and paragraph stating multiplicity one for p=2,3,5,7; Theorem 6.4, printed p.23

origin.inheritance_basis: Theorem 6.4 gives binomial(2*3-2,3-1)=6 with multiplicity; the introduction separately states all roots are simple for p=2,3,5,7.

notes: Haagerup explicitly recalls simplicity for these small primes. Simplicity for arbitrary prime length is not asserted.
